evals.name: ssm-access-denied-minimal-fix
evals.prompt:
Our web app container is failing at startup with this error:

An error occurred (AccessDeniedException) when calling the GetParametersByPath operation: User: arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/web-app-task/8f41c3f2 is not authorized to perform: ssm:GetParametersByPath on resource: arn:aws:ssm:eu-west-1:123456789012:parameter/apps/web/prod because no identity-based policy allows the ssm:GetParametersByPath action

The Terraform for the role is in this directory. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: The ReadAppParameters statement (or a new minimal statement) in iam.tf grants ssm:GetParametersByPath scoped to BOTH resource forms — arn:aws:ssm:eu-west-1:123456789012:parameter/apps/web/prod AND arn:aws:ssm:eu-west-1:123456789012:parameter/apps/web/prod/* — with no wildcard actions or resources. Nothing else in the policy changes.
expectations: The policy document in iam.tf now allows the ssm:GetParametersByPath action for the web-app-task role
The granted resources include both the bare path ARN (...parameter/apps/web/prod) and the path-wildcard ARN (...parameter/apps/web/prod/*)
No statement uses "*" as an action or as a resource
The fix stays in the aws_iam_policy_document data source style — no jsonencode() policy JSON is introduced
The WriteAppLogs statement and the assume-role policy are unchanged
The response explains the two-resource-form requirement for SSM path operations (why granting only one form still yields AccessDenied)

evals.name: cert-in-use-evidence-before-action
evals.prompt:
I'm trying to remove the old CloudFront setup and the stack has been stuck for an hour. It finally failed with:

DELETE_FAILED: Certificate arn:aws:acm:us-east-1:123456789012:certificate/2b7e5c9a-1f4d-4e26-9d3e-6f8a1b2c3d4e in use

I don't have the AWS console open right now. How do we fix this? I really don't want to lose the Cognito user pool that's in the same stack.
evals.expected_output: An evidence-first plan: read-only commands to run first (aws acm describe-certificate --certificate-arn ... --query 'Certificate.InUseBy' to find what still references the certificate, aws cloudformation describe-stack-events for the first FAILED event), then the fix — re-point or remove the referencing distribution/listener before the certificate can delete, ordering the change so the reference is released first. The Cognito user pool must be protected: set DeletionPolicy/RemovalPolicy Retain on it (or confirm it already retains) before any further delete attempts; at no point is force-deleting the stack or its stateful resources proposed as a first step.
expectations: The response provides the exact read-only command to find what holds the certificate (acm describe-certificate with the InUseBy query, or equivalent) before proposing any change
The response asks for or plans around the output of those commands rather than asserting what holds the certificate without evidence

The explanation identifies the general cause: a resource outside the delete set (e.g. a CloudFront distribution or listener) still references the certificate, and the reference must be released before deletion
The Cognito user pool is explicitly protected: a retain policy (DeletionPolicy: Retain / RemovalPolicy.RETAIN) is applied or verified before further destructive attempts
No step proposes deleting the stack, the user pool, or force-skipping resources as the first action
The plan ends with a verification step (delete completes, stack reaches a *_COMPLETE state)

evals.name: eventbridge-pattern-mismatch
evals.prompt: I just tried creating an S3 bucket through the manager and the create-bucket step function never fired. The rule and target are in events.tf, the code that publishes the event is publisher.py, and I captured one of the actual events off the bus with a debug rule — it's in captured-event.json. Why isn't this working?
evals.expected_output: Diagnosis: the rule pattern does not match the real event on two fields — detail-type (rule expects "bucket_create_requested", event carries "Bucket Create Requested") and detail.resource_type (rule expects detail.resource_type, event carries detail.resourceType). Fix: make pattern and producer agree on both fields (either side may be changed, but consistently), applied in the Terraform/producer code rather than the console. Verification via aws events test-event-pattern with the captured event, and checking the rule's FailedInvocations/target afterwards.
expectations: The detail-type mismatch between the rule pattern (bucket_create_requested) and the actual event (Bucket Create Requested) is identified, including that pattern matching is case-sensitive and exact
The second mismatch is identified: the pattern matches detail.resource_type but the event carries detail.resourceType
The fix changes the rule pattern and/or the publisher so BOTH fields agree consistently, in the source files (events.tf / publisher.py), not via console edits
The response suggests validating the corrected pattern against captured-event.json with aws events test-event-pattern (or an equivalent offline check)
The response notes the follow-on verification: confirm the target fires (rule Invocations/FailedInvocations metrics or a live end-to-end event) since a matching rule can still fail at the target
